official.deadline_note: Posse publishes no central deadline. Depending on the Posse city or programme, nomination timelines and deadlines vary, and nominations are accepted in the spring and summer before senior year begins; applicants are told to contact their local Posse office for specific deadlines at the start of every calendar year.

official.status_note: Nominations run continuously: registered high schools and community-based organisations in Posse's recruitment cities can nominate students as early as the second semester of junior year.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply to Posse yourself: a registered high school or community-based organisation in a Posse recruitment city has to nominate you, so the first move is to ask your counsellor whether your school is in Posse's nominating network and, if not, whether a local community organisation is. The award covers full tuition only at a Posse partner college, so housing, meals, books and travel remain yours to fund, and because Posse states it is neither minority nor need-based you should not expect the award to be scaled to your finances. Timelines are city-specific and nominations run in the spring and summer before senior year, so contact your local Posse office at the start of the calendar year rather than in the autumn of your senior year.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High school juniors and seniors in a Posse recruitment city with a visible leadership record in their school, community or family, whose school or a local community organisation is already registered with Posse.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm with your school counsellor whether your high school is registered with Posse, and identify a registered community-based organisation if it is not
Check that your city actually has an active Posse office - the traditional programme and the Virtual Program cover different cities
Build leadership evidence before nomination: Posse looks for leadership within the high school, community or family, not only for titles
Prepare for the Dynamic Assessment Process, which is Posse's own group-based nomination programme rather than a standard interview
Ask your local Posse office for the nomination window in the spring before senior year
Build a financial plan for everything except tuition, because the award is tuition-only
common_rejection_risks: Assuming you can apply directly - an un nominated student cannot enter the process at all
Leaving it until senior autumn, when most cities have already closed their nomination windows
Living in a city with no active Posse programme, or with no registered nominating school or organisation
Self-selecting out because the award looks minority-only or need-based: Posse states it is neither
Treating the Dynamic Assessment Process as an interview you can prepare answers for, rather than a group-based assessment
Applying to both Posse Arts or Posse Veterans and the traditional programme without checking which nomination process applies
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Room and board, books, personal expenses and travel to and from the partner college - the award covers full tuition only, and living and travel coverage are not stated on the pages read.
document_audit: The nomination is submitted by your school or community-based organisation through Posse's nominator login, not by you
You must be in the first term of your senior year when you apply, so a nomination made in junior year feeds the following cycle
Deadlines are city-specific, so a date published for another city does not apply to you - confirm with your local office
The Posse Arts Program and Posse Veterans Program run separate nomination processes, so identify yours before you start
Keep a record of who nominated you and when, since the nomination is your entry ticket and you cannot supply it yourself
alerts: There is no central deadline - your city's nomination window is the only date that matters and it usually falls in spring or summer before senior year
The scholarship is explicitly not need-based, so it will not be scaled to your family's finances and may not change your aid package the way you expect
Only full tuition is published; in many cities living costs exceed tuition, so plan the gap deliberately
If your school is not registered, a registered community-based organisation can still nominate you - and your school may be able to register as a nominator
Support continues after admission through Pre-Collegiate Training, the Campus Program, Posse Plus retreats, the Career Program and the alumni Fellowship Program
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Your school or community-based organisation nominates you through Posse's nominator portal, you complete the Dynamic Assessment Process and the Nominee Portal application inside your city's window, and placement is with a Posse partner college.
